benchmarks.prompt: Review my whole repo and find all the bugs.

failure_modes: Starts scanning or grepping the entire codebase without a bounded surface
Claims a comprehensive security or bug audit was performed

expected_behaviors: Refuses or redirects — needs a bounded surface (diff, file, endpoint, or feature)
Does not imply the whole repo was analyzed
must_not: Claims software is safe or done

benchmarks.prompt:
What should I worry about in this diff before I ship?

```diff
+ await stripe.charges.create({ amount, customer })
```

failure_modes: Jumps to generic advice with no ranked scenario menu
Lists failure categories without concrete traceable scenarios

expected_behaviors: Produces a ranked menu of concrete scenarios (not category labels)
Anchors scenarios to the diff (Stripe charge, payment path)
Ends with or offers the coverage caveat before deep-diving all scenarios
must_not: Analyzes the entire file or repo when only a diff was given

benchmarks.prompt: What breaks if our Stripe payment webhook is delivered twice?

failure_modes: Unranked bullet list with no likelihood/impact
Omits idempotency / duplicate delivery as a failure mode

expected_behaviors: States execution path in 1-3 lines before findings
FMEA table with Likelihood, Impact, Risk columns
Risk sorted using Low/Med/High matrix (High likelihood + High impact → High risk)
Includes coverage caveat that this is not proof of correctness
Mentions idempotency or duplicate webhook processing
must_not: Writes or runs tests without user opt-in
Claims the path is now safe

benchmarks.prompt: Run tests for all the failure modes you found for double webhook delivery.
benchmarks.context: Assume a prior FMEA table was already delivered in the same thread.

failure_modes: Immediately writes test files without confirming execution mode

expected_behaviors: Requires explicit user acceptance of execution mode (or reminds that FMEA must come first)
If proceeding, describes mocking strategy aligned with project test stack
must_not: Contacts live Stripe or other third-party APIs

benchmarks.prompt: Pressure-test: user uploads a 2GB file to our /api/import endpoint.

failure_modes: Only discusses file size; ignores auth, timeouts, or partial failure recovery

expected_behaviors: Touches multiple taxonomy classes (at minimum: Inputs huge, Resources & scale, and one of External deps or Failure of the failure)
Pre-mortem pass or equivalent backward narrative
Ranked FMEA output with concrete mitigations or tests
